status: Offline reference values for three-dimensional flight (DECISIONS A11); requires independent implementation checks. The planar file physics.json is unchanged and remains the planar regression.

reference_method.name: adaptive Dormand-Prince embedded 5(4), the planar file's stepper

trajectories_20000_s.independent_audit: separately coded pair-loop force and classical RK4, fixed 5 s step

trajectories_2000000_s.independent_audit: separately coded pair-loop force and classical RK4, fixed 10 s step

rigid_body.state: attitude quaternion and body rates; Euler's equations with qdot = q (0, omega)/2; quaternion normalised on output only
rigid_body.independent_audit: rotation matrix and inertial angular momentum (no quaternion, no Euler equation), classical RK4, fixed 0.05 s step

conventions.coordinates: right-handed Cartesian inertial x, y, z; one frame per case; vectors are [x, y, z]
conventions.reference_length: One universal r0 for every interacting pair; not reset at a new encounter or for a new body.
conventions.force: a_i = -sum_j GM_j*r0^(p-2)*(r_i-r_j)/|r_i-r_j|^(p+1), with |.| the three-dimensional distance
conventions.test_particle: ship has zero gravitational source mass; no thrust, drag, collisions or softening in these vectors
conventions.tolerance: absolute SI error; arrays compared component by component; scalar tolerance applies to every component; attitude compared after the sign alignment below
conventions.rotation: a case's rotation object gives the angles (rad) and matrix rows of R = Rz(node)*Rx(inclination)*Rz(argument) that turned the named planar case into this one
conventions.specific_angular_momentum: the vector r x v about the fixed source, m^2 s^-1
conventions.orbit_normal: unit vector along r x v about the fixed source
conventions.binary_specific_invariants: binary energy and angular momentum (a vector) divided by total binary mass; mass weights GM_i/sum(GM_i); no ship contribution
conventions.binary_angular_velocity: the circular binary's constant angular velocity vector, rad s^-1; binary_angular_frequency is its magnitude
conventions.ship_jacobi_constant: C = -2*Phi - |v|^2 + 2*omega_vec . (r x v) with r, v inertial barycentric and omega_vec the binary_angular_velocity; equal to 2*W - |v_rotating|^2 with W including z; valid only for a circular binary
conventions.about_primary: rho = r_ship - r_primary, u = v_ship - v_primary, n = (rho x u)/|rho x u|; ship_orbit_normal_about_primary = n; ship_node_longitude_about_primary = atan2(n_x, -n_y) in (-pi, pi]; ship_inclination_about_primary = acos(n_z); all osculating, measured against the inertial x-y plane, which is the binary's plane in those cases
conventions.ship_mean_nodal_rate_about_primary: (node_longitude(at_t) - node_longitude(0))/at_t with the difference wrapped into (-pi, pi]
conventions.plane_crossings: information only: reference times at which the ship's z changes sign
conventions.body_frame: right-handed; +x forward (roll axis), +y left (pitch axis), +z up (yaw axis)
conventions.attitude: unit quaternion [w, x, y, z], scalar first, Hamilton product, body to inertial: v_inertial = q * v_body * conj(q); (a * b) applies b first. q and -q are the same attitude: compare the rotation, not the sign (flip your q when its four-component dot product with the reference is negative, then compare components)
conventions.angular_velocity: body frame, rad s^-1; kinematics qdot = q * (0, omega_body) / 2
conventions.inertia: moments are the principal moments about principal x', y', z' through the centre of mass, kg m^2; axes is the unit quaternion turning principal-frame vectors into the body frame (identity: body axes are principal); inertia_tensor_body is the same tensor in body axes, rows
conventions.torque_body: constant torque about the centre of mass in body axes, N m
conventions.rotational_energy: omega . (J omega) / 2 with J the inertia tensor in body axes, J
conventions.angular_momentum_inertial: R(q) (J omega): the angular momentum about the centre of mass in inertial axes, kg m^2 s^-1
conventions.invariant_expectations: the analytic initial invariant repeated at each checkpoint, not the reference integrator's slightly drifted value
conventions.law_null: rigid_body cases have law: null; no gravity or gravity-gradient torque acts

cases.description: The binary in the x-y plane with a massless ship started on the unperturbed circular orbit of radius r0 about the primary, inclined 30 deg to the binary plane, node 40 deg. Long enough (2e6 s, about 32 ship orbits) for the secondary to turn the orbit's node by a measurable angle.
cases.claim_status: offline numerical reference; not a game demonstration

nodal_precession.unit: rad s^-1; negative is regression (the node moves against the orbit)
nodal_precession.note: The osculating node also oscillates at twice the binary's rate relative to the node, so the end-to-end value depends on where the run stops; the least-squares slope over the samples is the steadier measure. The expectation compares the end-to-end value because a consumer can form it from two states.

expect.basis: first-order secular formula -(p+1)*K2*cos(i)/(4*Omega*D^(p+1)); the tolerance is 10 % of it, see nodal_precession

cases.description: Torque-free body symmetric about body x (roll 6e4, pitch = yaw 5e5 kg m^2): steady precession. Values are the closed form.
cases.claim_status: offline reference for torque and attitude kinematics; not a game demonstration

closed_form.attitude: q(t) = q(L_hat, precession_rate*t) * q(0) * q(body x, relative_spin_rate*t), with q(axis, angle) = [cos(angle/2), sin(angle/2)*axis]

cases.description: Torque-free triaxial body (roll 7e4, pitch 5.5e5, yaw 4.5e5 kg m^2) tumbling near the unstable intermediate (yaw) axis; body axes are principal. High-accuracy numerical reference.
cases.claim_status: offline reference for torque and attitude kinematics; not a game demonstration

body_rate_closed_form.note: The initial rates are the Jacobi-elliptic solution at seed_time after a start with zero rate about the intermediate (yaw) axis, so the body rates at t are that solution at t + seed_time. The attitude has no elementary closed form and is numerical.

cases.description: The motion of spin-triaxial for a body whose principal frame is turned 0.35 rad from the body frame about (2/3, -1/3, 2/3): the inertia tensor in body axes is not diagonal. Values are spin-triaxial re-expressed: attitude = q_principal * conj(axes), rates = R(axes) rates_principal.
cases.claim_status: offline reference for torque and attitude kinematics; not a game demonstration

cases.description: From rest, a constant 40 N m body-frame torque about the pitch principal axis (5.5e5 kg m^2) of the triaxial body. Values are the closed form.
cases.claim_status: offline reference for torque and attitude kinematics; not a game demonstration

closed_form.attitude: q(t) = q(0) * q(body y, angular_acceleration*t^2/2); angular_velocity = angular_acceleration*t about body y
closed_form.note: Energy and angular momentum are not invariants here: the torque does work. Their expected values are the closed forms I*(alpha*t)^2/2 and I*alpha*t along the inertial direction of the torque axis, which stays fixed.
